title: Intel may expand 2 nm chip outsourcing to TSMC
gist: Market reports say Intel's Nova Lake desktop parts will lead with bLLC large last-level cache built on a mix of Intel 18A and TSMC N2P, while the follow-on Razor Lake generation may add TSMC's high-performance N2X — extending Intel's TSMC dependence deeper into 2nm. Beyond TSMC, the second-order beneficiaries named are Taiwanese CMP consumables suppliers, with CSST posting Q2 revenue of NT$2.49bn (+17.9% YoY), 40.1% gross margin and NT$3.49 EPS on fast-growing 2nm and 1.6nm diamond-disc shipments.

insights.claim: Intel's next-generation Nova Lake desktop processors are reported to prioritize bLLC large last-level cache, with laptop versions possibly delayed to the subsequent Razor Lake-HX generation.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: A desktop-first cache strategy with a mobile delay shifts Intel's competitive timing in notebooks — the segment where AMD's cache advantage has been most visible.

insights.claim: Razor Lake is rumored to use TSMC's high-performance 2nm N2X process, which if it reaches mass production would mean Intel's collaboration with TSMC on advanced processes extends to a wider range of 2nm products.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Each additional Intel tile moved to TSMC is incremental leading-edge revenue for TSMC and a reduction in Intel's internal wafer loading — directly relevant to Intel Foundry utilization math.
insights.quote: Razor Lake is rumored to utilize TSMC's high-performance 2nm N2X process.
insights.locator: More notably, Razor Lake is rumored

insights.claim: Supply chain sources indicate Nova Lake, slated for release early next year, will use a combination of process technologies including Intel's own 18A and TSMC's N2P, with Razor Lake potentially adding N2X on top.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Confirms a multi-foundry tile strategy is now Intel's baseline rather than an exception — structurally caps how much of Intel's own product volume 18A/14A can recapture.

insights.claim: Industry analysts read Intel's outsourcing of some compute chips to TSMC as risk mitigation against relying on a single process technology, given challenges in high-end CPU launch schedules, performance and production capacity even as Intel pushes its own 18A.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Frames the outsourcing as a hedge rather than a surrender — but it also means Intel's product margins stay exposed to TSMC's leading-edge wafer pricing.

insights.claim: bLLC stands for Big Last-Level Cache, and by increasing last-level cache capacity it reduces the latency of accessing system memory — a strategy chip industry analysts see as directly targeting AMD's 3D V-Cache technology.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Sets up a direct architectural contest in gaming and latency-sensitive desktop workloads where AMD's V-Cache parts have held pricing power.
insights.locator: bLLC stands for Big Last-Level Cache

themes.theme: N2X process mechanics and CMP intensity

insights.claim: N2X is a high-performance extension of TSMC's N2 platform aimed at high-frequency CPUs, AI and HPC applications, shifting transistor technology from FinFET to nanosheets and raising the precision required in thin-film deposition, etching, cleaning and CMP planarization.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: The FinFET-to-nanosheet transition raises process-step intensity — a direct volume tailwind for deposition, etch, clean and CMP equipment and consumables suppliers.

insights.claim: As processes shrink to 2 nanometers, requirements for wafer surface flatness and defect control increase, driving a simultaneous rise in the number of CMP polishing operations and in the value of high-end consumables.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: CMP consumables revenue scales faster than wafer starts at advanced nodes — a leveraged way to express a 2nm-ramp view without owning the foundry.
insights.locator: As manufacturing processes shrink to 2 nanometers

insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: A concentrated local supplier with semis now two-thirds of revenue is a high-beta proxy on TSMC's advanced-node ramp.

insights.claim: Chung-Shock Technology (CSST) has mastered CMP diamond discs and reclaimed wafers, and the more advanced the process node, the higher the requirements for diamond particle uniformity, lifespan and defect control.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Node-driven specification tightening means ASP expansion, not just unit growth — the margin mechanism behind the reported gross-margin lift.
